newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese 120,000 tonnes/yr copper bar line starts.
newsitem.headline: Chinese 120,000 tonnes/yr copper bar line starts.

text.p: A joint venture between a Chinese and a Taiwanese firm has started a new copper bar production line with output of 120,000 tonnes a year, company officials said on Wednesday.
The Nanjing Walsin Wire and Cable Corp, 71 percent owned by Taiwan's Walsin Lihwa Corp went into operation on Monday, aiming export 30 percent of production, an official said by telephone.
Nanjing Walsin, in Nangjing city in eastern Jiangsu province, will buy much of the 120,000 tonnes of raw copper it needed from abroad, the official said.

Japan's Marubeni Corp and Itochu Corp each had a 10 percent stake in the company, while Nanjing Xingang Development Co, the Nanjing Telecommunications Bureau, and the Nanjing Electricity Supply Bureau were the Chinese partners in the firm, he said.
The production equipment was purchased from a U.S. firm, he said but gave no details of the deal.
